ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: Given: As shown in the figure, $AB$ is the diameter of $\odot O$, the chord $CD$ intersects $AB$ at point E, $BE=1$, $AE=5$, and $\angle AEC=30^\circ$. What is the length of $CD$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure, draw $OF\perp CD$ at F, and connect OD, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle OFE=90^\circ$, $CD=2FD$, \\
$\because$ $\angle AEC=30^\circ$, \\
$\therefore$ $OF=\frac{1}{2}OE$, \\
$\because$ BE=1, AE=5, \\
$\therefore$ AB=BE+AE=6, \\
$\because$ AB is the diameter, \\
$\therefore$ $OB=OD=\frac{1}{2}AB=3$, \\
$\therefore$ $OE=OB-BE=2$, \\
$\therefore$ $OF=\frac{1}{2}OE=1$, \\
$\therefore$ $DF=\sqrt{OD^2-OF^2}=2\sqrt{2}$, \\
$\therefore$ $CD=2DF=\boxed{4\sqrt{2}}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is a circle, and the horizontal line segment AB passes through the center O of the circle, with A at the right end and B at the left end, so AB is a diameter. Point E is on AB, located between B and O. The oblique chord CD passes through E, with D on the lower-left side of the circle and C on the upper-right side of the circle; the ray from E to C forms the given 30° angle with the horizontal EA. Reasoning: It is known that BE=1 and AE=5, so AB=BE+AE=6. Because AB is the diameter of the circle, the radius OB=OD=AB/2=3. Point E is between B and O, and BE=1, so OE=OB-BE=3-1=2. According to the method, draw OF perpendicular to chord CD at F. Because chord CD and AB form 30° at E, in right triangle OEF, OF=OE·sin30°=2·1/2=1. The perpendicular from the center of the circle to a chord bisects the chord, so CD=2DF. Also OD is a radius, OD=3, and in right triangle ODF, DF=sqrt(OD^2-OF^2)=sqrt(3^2-1^2)=sqrt(8)=2sqrt(2). Therefore CD=2DF=4sqrt(2).
